details.purpose: To record details about the provision of physical assistance at clinically relevant events in the intervention lifecycle, from planning to completion, and including deviations or interruptions.
details.use:
Use to record details about the provision of physical assistance at clinically relevant events in the intervention lifecycle, from planning to completion, and including deviations or interruptions.
The scope of this data group includes a wide range of physical assistance, including but not limited to activities of daily living: - Mobility assistance – such as walking, standing, or transferring - Personal activities and hygiene – such as bathing, dressing, grooming, and toileting. - Feeding assistance - Therapeutic exercises – such as hands-on support during physical therapy exercises or rehabilitation activities - Use of assistive devices – such as helping with the use of mobility aids, prosthetic device, or communication devices.
Record one instance per careflow step or event for each specified assistance activity in a health record. If the assistance consists of a single activity, the 'Assistance provided' and the 'Assistance completed' careflow step may be recorded simultaneously. However, if the assistance consists of multiple component activities, record a separate instance of the 'Assistance provided' careflow step for each component activity provided, and record the 'Assistance completed' step only after the final component activity has been provided.
details.misuse: Not to be used to record other types of assistance, other than physical or hands-on support. The need for a specific archetype for this purpose is acknowledged but has not yet been developed.

items.items: Physical assistance

Hands-on support provided by a caregiver to enable an individual to complete a task they cannot perform independently and/or safely due to a limitation in strength, mobility, coordination, communication, cognition, or sensory abilities, such as visual or auditory impairments.
Item tree
@ internal @
Assistance type
Name of the specific type of physical support or help required.

For example: washing hair, toileting, transfer from wheelchair to car, or use of a communication device. Use of a clinical terminology is recommended whenever possible. Free text entry should be allowed only when an appropriate coded value is not available.
Assistance category
An overarching grouping for the assistance identified in 'Assistance type'.
For example: activity of daily living, mobilty.
Description
Narrative description about the physical assistance, relevant to the active careflow step.
Clinical indication
The clinical reason for the physical assistance.
For example: diabetes control; or cancer treatment. Coding of the indication with a terminology is preferred, where possible. This data element allows multiple occurrences.
Additional details
Additional structured details about the physical assistance.
Scheduled date/time
The intended date and/or time for provision of the physical assistance.
This data element must only be used in conjunction with the 'Assistance scheduled' careflow step.
Comment
Additional narrative about the physical assistance activity or careflow step not captured in other fields.
Assistance planned
An intent or need to initiate the assistance process has been recognised; active careflow steps have not commenced.
Assistance request sent
A request to initiate the assistance process has been submitted; active careflow steps have not commenced.
Assistance postponed
The planned assistance has been temporarily stopped; active careflow steps have not commenced.
Item tree
@ internal @
Assistance cancelled
The planned assistance has been permanently stopped; active careflow steps have not commenced.
Assistance scheduled
A date and/or time has been scheduled for the planned assistance; active careflow steps have not commenced.
Assistance provided
The assistance has been provided; active careflow steps are in process.

If the assistance consists of a single component, this careflow step and the 'Assistance completed' step may be recorded simultaneously. If the assistance consists of multiple components, record a separate instance of this careflow step for each component provided, and record the 'Assistance completed' step only after the final component has been delivered.
Assistance suspended
The active assistance process has been temporarily stopped; active careflow steps have been put on hold.
Assistance abandoned
The active assistance process has been permanently stopped; active careflow steps have been aborted.
Assistance completed
All components of the assistance have been delivered; active careflow steps have been completed.
If the assistance consists of a single component, this careflow step and the 'Assistance supply delivered' step may be recorded simultaneously.
Requestor order identifier
The local ID assigned to the order by the 'Requestor'.
Requestor
Details about the healthcare provider or organisation requesting the order.
Receiver order identifier
The ID assigned to the order by the 'Receiver'.
This may also be referred to as 'Filler order identifier'.
Receiver
Details about the healthcare provider or organisation who received the request.
Extension
Additional information required to extend the model with local content or to align with other reference models or formalisms.
For example: local information requirements; or additional metadata to align with FHIR.
Outcome
The result or consequence of the assistance provided, reflecting the individual's ability to complete the activity with the support.

For example: completed successfully, partially completed, unable to complete, or ineffective. This data element must only be used in conjunction with the 'Assistance provided' or 'Assistance completed' careflow step.
